comment: Edits on fetched sources, each must match exactly once. tree: ath12k (drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k) or freebsd (repository root). Edited FreeBSD headers go to an overlay searched first. LinuxKPI edits lx-device-of-node, lx-bss-conf-fields, lx-reg-rule-psd, lx-channel-psd and lx-regd-sync-copies are adapted from hackios wifi/lx/patches (MIT), see xnu/fuxi-ath12k/compat/PROVENANCE.md.

LinuxKPI bug: size_mul() is given one argument, so kmalloc_objs() cannot compile; kzalloc_objs() has it right.
edits.replace: kmalloc(size_mul((_n), sizeof(typeof(_p))), default_gfp(__VA_ARGS__))

edits.why: See ath12k-rx-refill-guard-a.
Design section 4: the address given to iOS at attach, before the radio exists, must be the radio's; mac.c has no device-address fallback.
LinuxKPI's cfg80211_find_ie() answers NULL always with a TODO; mac.c's beacon parsing needs the element. Same walk as cfg80211_find_elem() beside it.
There is no mesh here, so false is the true answer. dp_tx.c asks for each frame: with TODO() logging on (fa_80211.c) this would flood the log.
LinuxKPI refuses silently (SKB_TODO is compiled out). Buffers cannot grow here; the failure is ath12k's to handle but must show in the log.
As lx-pskb-expand-says. Design section 4 keeps hw->extra_tx_headroom free so TX should not get here.
Design M1: stop after HTC ready through ath12k_core_start's normal error path.

Design M2: stop once the radio is registered, with WMI ready and hw_mode behind it, before the data rings are set up. What ath12k_mac_register() did is undone, then the error path below it and the caller's ath12k_core_stop() run.
Design M2: upstream error lines must be absent when the stage stops as planned. Any other failure still says it.
edits.replace:
if (ret != -ECANCELED)
				ath12k_warn(ab, "unable to start hw group\n");

edits.why: Design section 9: LinuxKPI's IEEE80211_EHT_PHY_CAP* and PPE threshold values are running counters, so this function would filter the wrong bits and offer the result. eht_cap stays zero, has_eht false. linuxkpi_80211_wiphy_register() refuses a radio that offers it.

Design M2: WMI_INIT and service_ready_ext on this CNSS-class image are unknown offline, and a silent firmware leaves only a timeout. The boot shows which events came, in order. Says only the first ones.

Design M4: the scan runs where everything is up, at the end of the hardware group's start, and stops through its error label: ath12k_core_hw_group_stop() (unregister, data rings, destroy), then the caller's ath12k_core_stop() and MODE off. Nothing it needs takes ag->mutex, which is held here.
Design section 6, fuxiath12kq: whether the hw mode command is what upsets a firmware at its first radio work. Without the knob, as upstream.

Design section 4 keeps upstream's scan link 15 first. Link 15 has no link configuration, so ath12k_mac_setup_vdev_params_mbssid() returns -ENOLINK unless the firmware has WMI_TLV_SERVICE_MBSS_PARAM_IN_VDEV_START_SUPPORT: certain to fail, so only then the interface's own link 0 is used. fa_hif.c logs which.

w-m4: every channel list had 2.4 GHz only. For a radio with both 5 and 6 GHz (one WCN7850 radio) this function sets the 5 GHz range only if the radio has no 6 GHz, and relies on the 6 GHz branch to cover 5 GHz by widening the range to 7125 MHz. A domain without a 6 GHz rule (CN here) leaves reg_freq_6ghz.end_freq 0, so that branch does nothing and the range stays at 2.4 GHz. ath12k_mac_setup_channels_rates() does not have this condition, which is why the first range was right. The 5 GHz branch now runs for any radio that registered a 5 GHz band.
edits.replace:
if (supported_bands & WMI_HOST_WLAN_5GHZ_CAP &&
	    (!ar->supports_6ghz || ar->mac.sbands[NL80211_BAND_5GHZ].channels)) {

edits.why: Design M4 sends nothing beyond what the one scan needs. With PREPARING left unset, hw_scan does not start the firmware's periodic 11d country scan, whose answer could also change the regulatory domain under this stage. This code is only reached on stages 4 and 5.
Design M4: a firmware that stops answering shows only as a timeout here. Stage 4 notes each command and result, and takes a timeout as the firmware's death; stages 1 and 2 return at once.

w-ios1 panicked under load after msdu_done failures: a stale destination descriptor is the theory. dst_num_free() with sync updates cached_hp, and try_again then sees hp == cached_hp and skips this barrier: rx_process starts with done = false, so an empty poll goes that way. Always order the head pointer before the descriptor.
The same order for the other reader of a destination ring head pointer.
A descriptor whose buffer was already reaped has no skb, and rxcb would be read from NULL. Counted and said, so a run shows whether descriptors are seen twice.
The same dereference on the REO exception path.
The same dereference where an exception buffer is dropped.
The same dereference on the WBM error path.
w-ios1 said this about nine times before the panic. Counted beside the stale count, so the next run shows whether they go together. The warning stays.
edits.find: ath12k_warn(dp->ab, "msdu_done bit in msdu_end is not set\n");
edits.replace:
fa_rx_msdu_not_done();
		ath12k_warn(dp->ab, "msdu_done bit in msdu_end is not set\n");
